title: Domains and normalized data for the compact-support double transpose
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be separated finite-type morphisms between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], without an absolute separatedness assumption. Choose compactifications of $f,g,gf$, with nonnegative integer bounds on the dimensions of their proper ambient schemes [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Work in ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Put $S_h=Lh^*$, $P_h=Rh_!$, $G_h=Rh^!$ and $W_h=G_hA$, for $h=f,g,gf$, using [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Use the bounded-below etale-origin Hom bijections, with their chosen-compactification normalization, and their counits $\epsilon_h$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Suppose $W_f,W_g\in D^b_{ctf}$ and the counit/projection tensor maps $\theta_{h,B}:S_hB\otimes_A^LW_h\to G_hB$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness] are isomorphisms for $h=f,g$ and every $B\in D^b_{ctf}$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, the objects $G_gK$, $S_gK\otimes_A^LW_g$ and
$$N=S_f(S_gK\otimes_A^LW_g)\otimes_A^LW_f$$
are bounded constructible finite-Tor objects with bounded-below etale-origin witnesses. Every module input and tensor input of the double-transpose expressions below is bounded constructible and of etale origin, as is its compact-support image; every coefficient input is finite Tor. Thus the bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(N,G_fG_gK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(P_fN,G_gK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(P_gP_fN,K)$$
and their instances at $W_g$ and the coefficient units are defined, natural and injective.

Let $\alpha:P_gP_f\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{gf}$ be the canonical compactification compositor [thm-sf-comp-composition], and let $c:G_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fG_g$ be its adjunction conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Through $\alpha$, its counit is $\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$. In particular
$$q=c_{A_Z}^{-1}\circ\theta_{f,W_g}:S_fW_g\otimes_A^LW_f\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{gf}$$
is an isomorphism.

For $h=f,g,gf$, $B\in D^b_{ctf}$ on its target and $M\in D^b_c$ on its source, let $\pi^h_{B,M}:P_h(S_hB\otimes_A^LM)\to B\otimes_A^LP_hM$ be the inverse of the specified projection map of [def-exchange-projection], conjugated by tensor symmetry. On all the objects, arrows and naturality instances occurring in the two expressions
$$\theta_{f,G_gK}\circ(S_f\theta_{g,K}\otimes1),\qquad c_K\circ\theta_{gf,K}\circ(1\otimes q),$$
these inverse projections exist and satisfy the unit and coefficient-associativity equations [def-sfb-projection-formula], using the canonical monoidal pullback comparisons. For every $M\in D^b_c(X,A)$, under $\alpha$ they satisfy
$$\pi^{gf}_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\circ P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M}).$$
In particular all domain, naturality, projection-coherence and composite-adjunction hypotheses of the restricted-domain double-transpose calculation are satisfied on these expressions.

proof.text: Pullback preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ with its Tor interval, and tensoring two such objects adds their Tor intervals. Starting with $K,W_g,W_f$, apply these two statements successively: $S_gK$, $U=S_gK\otimes W_g$, $S_fU$, $S_fW_g$, and $N=S_fU\otimes W_f$ are in $D^b_{ctf}$. The assumed isomorphism $\theta_{g,K}:U\cong G_gK$ puts $G_gK$ in the same full subcategory; then $S_fG_gK\otimes W_f$ and, by the assumed $\theta_{f,G_gK}$, $G_fG_gK$ are in it. At the units the argument applies because the constant coefficient unit is constructible with Tor interval $[0,0]$: tensoring with it is the identity. For arbitrary bounded constructible module input $M$, tensoring with any of these finite-Tor coefficients remains bounded constructible by clause (i) of the tensor lemma. This also covers the coefficient products and reassociations in the projection laws. No finite Tor amplitude is inferred for an arbitrary bounded constructible module. The Lean auxiliary membership lemmas use the already proved fixed-scalar etale tensor and upper-star stability theorems, reflecting Tor amplitude with torAmplitudeIn_of_mapDerivedCategory and transporting back with the canonical derived comparison tensor and pullback isomorphisms. Strict fullness transports the smooth exceptional image along asIso theta. This does not require an intrinsic tensor construction.

proof.text: Every bounded constructible object in Step 1 has a bounded constructible etale representative by the constructible-origin equivalence. Fixed-scalar compact-support finiteness sends each bounded constructible module input for $f,g,gf$ to a bounded constructible object of etale origin. Apply it also to $P_fM$ for $g$, and to the tensor module inputs of Step 1. Thus $P_fN$ and $P_gP_fN$, and the analogous inputs at $W_g$ and at the units, are in the bounded-below comparison classes. This checks every module input by its form: finite successive pullbacks and tensors covered in Step 1, or compact-support images of those objects. No Tor claim about these compact-support images is needed.

proof.text:
Use the normalized Hom bijections of the ambient-adjoint-class theorem for $f$ at $(N,G_gK)$, then for $g$ at $(P_fN,K)$. Steps 1--2 verify their domains. They are natural bijections, hence their composite is injective. The composite-adjunction formula gives counit $e_K=\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$. Compact-support composition preserves the comparison class and gives the specified $\alpha$. Its conjugate is the indicated $c$, with
$$e_K\circ P_gP_f(c_K)=\epsilon_{gf,K}\circ\alpha_{G_{gf}K}.$$
Here conjugacy is on the comparison class. The right adjoints are the etale-origin objects $\nu^*h^\times R\nu_*L$ of the ambient theorem and remain bounded below. The two natural representing Hom bijections and $\alpha$ give inverse representing maps: transpose the identity of either representing object; naturality makes the composites transpose to identities, and injectivity makes them inverse. Finite-site transport identifies this conjugate and these counits with the specified ones. At $A_Z$, $\theta_{f,W_g}$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis and $c_{A_Z}$ is one by this argument. Thus $q=c_{A_Z}^{-1}\theta_{f,W_g}$ is an isomorphism. The Lean auxiliary hom_natural proof is the explicit Hom-chain calculation: fullness of derived comparison lifts an ambient source map to the two chosen etale origins, fixedCompactSupportComparisonIso naturality identifies the left square, and the two ordinary adjunction Hom-equivalences give left and right naturality. Applying injectivity then identifies inverse transposition with image of the arrow followed by the specified counit. The subsequent composite-conjugate argument in this step remains to be formalized.

proof.text: Choose etale representatives for the bounded constructible inputs. Tor comparison reflects the coefficient Tor intervals to their representatives. The finite compact-support projection theorem applies to each bounded constructible module representative and finite-Tor coefficient representative. It gives invertibility and naturality of the proper counit projection followed by the open tensor map, also for pro-etale realizations. Finite-site transport pins it to the transformation of [def-exchange-projection]. Inverting and conjugating by tensor symmetry gives exactly $\pi^h_{B,M}$. The coefficients required are $G_gK$, $S_gK\otimes W_g$, $W_g$, $K$, the coefficient units and their finite products and pullbacks; Step 1 verifies finite Tor for all. Natural transformations restrict to arrows between these full domains, so all the required naturality instances are defined.

proof.text:
For $h=pj$ the specified forward projection, after symmetry, is the composite of the left-coefficient proper action for $p^*\dashv Rp_*$ and the left-coefficient open action for $j_!\dashv j^*$. Ringed-derived comparisons make these pullbacks symmetric strong monoidal with the specified composition maps. The proper-action lemma supplies its unit and coefficient-associativity equations. Open normalization says that $j_!$ is fully faithful, its unit is invertible, and the tensor comparison restricts to the identity under that unit. These are precisely the hypotheses of the open-action lemma, which supplies the same equations for the specified open map. Apply the composite-action lemma with $(F,R)=(p^*,Rp_*)$ and $(Q,J)=(j^*,j_!)$. Its composite is the map $B\otimes P_hM\to P_h(S_hB\otimes M)$ defined in [def-exchange-projection], so both forward action laws hold. All needed components are invertible by Step 4. Inverting the unit equation gives the unit law for $\pi$. Inverting the associativity equation reverses the factors and gives
$$\alpha_{B,B',P_hM}\pi^h_{B\otimes B',M}
=(1_B\otimes\pi^h_{B',M})\pi^h_{B,S_hB'\otimes M}P_h(\alpha_{S_hB,S_hB',M}(\delta_{B,B'}\otimes1)).$$
This is the equation of [def-sfb-projection-formula], with the same monoidal comparisons.

proof.text:
Apply ordinary-etale compact projection coherence to etale representatives of $M,K$. Its graph-factorization comparison $E:P_{gf}^e\to P_g^eP_f^e$ is built from refinement comparisons and proper/open interchanges in one compatible compactification tower; on bounded-below etale inputs, the choice-independence of the canonical etale compositor therefore identifies $E$ with the inverse of that compositor $\alpha^e$, which is the etale compositor used by site coherence, and its displayed equation compares the successive inverse projections with the inverse projection for $gf$. Compact-support site coherence carries this compositor to the specified $\alpha$; finite-site transport carries each projection to the specified pro-etale map. The monoidal comparisons carry its tensor reassociations to those used here. Thus, identifying source and target through $\alpha$ and the pullback compositor, the equality is
$$\pi^{gf}_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\circ P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M}).$$
Step 2 gives a bounded constructible etale representative of $P_fM$, and Step 1 gives finite Tor for $S_gK$, so every component exists. Steps 3--5 give the other domain, naturality, unit, associativity and adjunction hypotheses of the restricted double transpose.
